messages.text: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for AI without making unsupported claims?

### Short answer
The current passages do not support an AI-specific competitor comparison for a Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution; to avoid unsupported claims, you need formal R&S product evidence, official competitor evidence, AI-use-case evidence, and validation or test-report evidence that directly ties those items together [1][14][18][61].
### Evidence required
You need an AI-specific test requirement or use-case document, because the AI server ecosystem source is only a sales / solution mapping and does not represent formal product configuration, customer relationship, or validated opportunity [1].
You need formal R&S specifications, features, option codes, and configuration evidence, because the CMX500 page distinguishes binding specifications from feature overviews and notes that data without tolerance limits is not binding [69].
You need the exact signaling scope from formal R&S documents, because CMX500 is documented as a universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution for LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, and TDD device testing [7][8].
You need the exact non-signaling scope from formal or validated sources, because the callbox material lists non-signaling verification as a use case but also says multiple use cases lack complete option stack, BOM, DUT conditions, or test reports [75][74].
You need option-level evidence for signaling claims, because the passages list CMX500 signaling options for WLAN, LTE, NR, RedCap, NTN, and related extensions with option codes and order numbers [71][72].
You need automation and interface evidence if comparing workflow, because the passages identify CMsquares, CMXmars, CMsequencer, XLAPI, and SCPI as CMX500 interfaces and automation paths [73].
You need separate formal evidence for production or factory-line non-signaling claims, because the Amarisoft battle card links R&S production scaling to CMP180, CMP200, and CMW100 K06 but says each production platform specification must be cited separately [79][21].
You need competitor official documentation or third-party evidence, because the Amarisoft comparison page says R&S battle-card claims about Amarisoft have only a single R&S internal source and should be checked against Amarisoft official material and third-party evidence for customer documents [14].
You need competitor official documentation or third-party evidence for Anritsu, because the Anritsu comparison page says R&S battle-card claims mainly come from an internal battle card and should be checked against Anritsu official data and third-party evidence [18].
You may use the Anritsu MX844030PC brochure only for Anritsu product facts, because it supports that MX844030PC is a Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ, and RF-IF configurations [55][57].
You cannot use Anritsu’s MX844030PC brochure to prove R&S superiority, because the Anritsu comparison page says that brochure can describe Anritsu products but cannot verify R&S advantage claims [18].
You need validation reports, test-case lists, option codes, versions, and accreditation or certification evidence for PTCRB / GCF / operator-acceptance claims, because the Amarisoft battle card lacks those details for R&S aligned tests and Samsung-related NTN validation claims [20].
You must not equate CMX500 RF pre-conformance with strict conformance or certification, because the RF pre-conformance page says strict RF conformance testing and validated test cases use the R&S TS8980 Conformance Test Platform [50].
You need formal test setup, DUT, band combination, software release, and report evidence for throughput or performance claims, because the CMX500 callbox unresolved section says the 10.6 Gbps and 10 Gbps claims lack those details [37].
You need formal datasheets or verified test reports for FR1 / FR2 / FR3 bandwidth and data-rate comparisons, because the Anritsu comparison page flags bandwidth and data-rate limitations and contradictions as requiring formal validation [18].
You need formal test setup, option, fixture, frequency, and sales-kit content for AI-server mapping claims, because the AI-server R&S solution mapping table explicitly says those details are not provided [3].
You need official competitor support, warranty, calibration, and footprint evidence before using those as differentiators, because the Amarisoft unresolved page says “no global footprint,” “remote-only support,” and similar claims require Amarisoft official or third-party confirmation [89].
You need TCO, calibration-count, license-count, or throughput calculations before making cost or productivity claims, because the Anritsu offensive-play page says fewer boxes, fewer calibrations, fewer licenses, lower TCO, and higher throughput are sales messages without a TCO formula [81].

AISeverEcosystem R&S solution mapping › 與既有知識的關係
- [[R&S PCB test solutions]] 提供 2026.3.4 R&S high-speed digital 簡報中的 PCB fabricator / system house 測試流程；本頁則來自市場 Excel，將 R&S 儀器與 AI server supply-chain 類別做銷售 mapping。
- [[高頻高速 PCB 測試解決方案]] 與 [[Dk-Df]]、[[Delta-L]]、[[TDR 阻抗測量]] 已有 Keysight / PCB test 圖像來源；本頁新增 R&S 方案對應，但未提供可替代正式規格的量測條件。
- [[AI 伺服器 PCB 供應鏈升級]] 記錄材料與板層升級；本頁只補充對應測試入口，例如 IL、TDR、high speed trace、PDN Target Z。

Anritsu MX844030PC
[[Anritsu MX844030PC]] 是 Anritsu 的 **Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software**，用於在 PC / virtual environment 中執行 NR / RedCap protocol stack simulation 與 protocol testing。

Anritsu MX844030PC › Interface / configuration
來源列出三種主要 interface / configuration：

| Configuration | 用途 | 主要 items |
|---|---|---|
| MAC-IF for NR/RedCap | NR / RedCap MAC interface | MX844030PC、MX844030PC-PL011、MX844030PC-PL012、MX844030PC-TL011、MX844030PC-TL012 |
| PHY-IF Digital-IQ for RedCap | RedCap Digital-IQ / PHY interface | MX844030PC、MX844030PC-PL001、MX844030PC-TL001 |
| RF-IF for RedCap | RedCap RF real-time interface | MX844030PC、[[Anritsu MD8190A]]、MD8190A-001、[[MX819020A]]、MX819020A-020 |

來源文字說明 MAC / PHY Digital IQ interfaces 為 non real-time，RF interface 為 real-time 且使用 Anritsu SDR Unit。

mx844030pc-j1200 › 重點摘要
- [[Anritsu MX844030PC]] 被描述為 **Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software**，屬於 [[Virtual Signalling Tester]] / software protocol simulator，用於在 PC 上虛擬化 protocol stack。
- 來源說明此 solution 透過在 PC 上重現 [[RRC-NAS]]、[[PDCP]]、[[RLC]]、[[MAC]] 等 protocol layers，不使用一般硬體測試儀即可建立 protocol test environment；但在 RF interface configuration 中仍會使用 [[Anritsu MD8190A]] SDR / Universal RF Unit 與 [[MX819020A]] RF platform。
- 來源定位其對 [[Beyond 5G]]、[[6G]]、[[5G]]、[[LTE]]、[[IoT]]、[[5G RedCap]]、Automotive、Healthcare、Industrial IoT、Smart Cities 等應用的虛擬化測試需求有用。
- 來源把解決方案分成 Pre-silicon / Post-silicon 用途：Pre-silicon 強調 [[Shift-Left]]、EDA / PC 上 DUT、MAC / PHY Digital IQ interface；Post-silicon 強調 IoT device / communication module 的 basic protocol test、sample scenarios、test procedure 設定與 report / log 顯示。
- 來源明示介面選項包含 **MAC-IF for NR/RedCap**、**PHY-IF Digital-IQ for RedCap**、**RF-IF for RedCap**。
- 來源說明 software-based architecture 可使用一般 PC 快速建置，並可使用 MAC / PHY Digital-IQ / RF 等 IF 在不同開發階段驗證；使用 common [[RTD]] GUI 可將 Post-Silicon phase 的 NR protocol test cases 移植到 Pre-silicon phase。
- RF real-time configuration 使用 [[Anritsu MD8190A]] Universal RF Unit。其規格包含 TDD 0.4 GHz to 6 GHz、FDD 0.4 GHz to 2.7 GHz、最大解析頻寬 100 MHz、最大輸入 +23 dBm CW、設定輸入 / 輸出 level 與 nominal ±3 dB accuracy。
- 推薦 PC 為 **DELL OptiPlex XE4 Small Form Factor**，OS 為 Ubuntu 20.04 LTS，CPU 需 Intel Core i7 12700 以上且支援 AVX2，Memory 需 16 Gbyte 以上，SSD 512 Gbyte 以上，並需追加 1G NIC ST1000SPEXD4 與 10G NIC X520-10G-2S-X8-D。
- Ordering information 列出 [[Anritsu MX844030PC]] 本體、PL/TL license、support service、[[Anritsu MD8190A]]、[[MX819020A]]、[[Z1320G]]、[[MT8000A-AK003]]、[[Z1591A]]、[[J1440A]]、[[G0408A]]、[[J1581A]] 等品項。

### Short answer
The current passages do not support an AI-specific competitor comparison for a Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution; to avoid unsupported claims, you need formal R&S product evidence, official competitor evidence, AI-use-case evidence, and validation or test-report evidence that directly ties those items together [1][14][18][61].
### Evidence required
You need an AI-specific test requirement or use-case document, because the AI server ecosystem source is only a sales / solution mapping and does not represent formal product configuration, customer relationship, or validated opportunity [1].
You need formal R&S specifications, features, option codes, and configuration evidence, because the CMX500 page distinguishes binding specifications from feature overviews and notes that data without tolerance limits is not binding [69].
You need the exact signaling scope from formal R&S documents, because CMX500 is documented as a universal one-box network emulation and measurement test solution for LTE, NR FR1, NR FR2, NSA, SA, FDD, and TDD device testing [7][8].
You need the exact non-signaling scope from formal or validated sources, because the callbox material lists non-signaling verification as a use case but also says multiple use cases lack complete option stack, BOM, DUT conditions, or test reports [75][74].
You need option-level evidence for signaling claims, because the passages list CMX500 signaling options for WLAN, LTE, NR, RedCap, NTN, and related extensions with option codes and order numbers [71][72].
You need automation and interface evidence if comparing workflow, because the passages identify CMsquares, CMXmars, CMsequencer, XLAPI, and SCPI as CMX500 interfaces and automation paths [73].
You need separate formal evidence for production or factory-line non-signaling claims, because the Amarisoft battle card links R&S production scaling to CMP180, CMP200, and CMW100 K06 but says each production platform specification must be cited separately [79][21].
You need competitor official documentation or third-party evidence, because the Amarisoft comparison page says R&S battle-card claims about Amarisoft have only a single R&S internal source and should be checked against Amarisoft official material and third-party evidence for customer documents [14].
You need competitor official documentation or third-party evidence for Anritsu, because the Anritsu comparison page says R&S battle-card claims mainly come from an internal battle card and should be checked against Anritsu official data and third-party evidence [18].
You may use the Anritsu MX844030PC brochure only for Anritsu product facts, because it supports that MX844030PC is a Virtual Signalling Tester NR Software with MAC-IF, PHY-IF Digital-IQ, and RF-IF configurations [55][57].
You cannot use Anritsu’s MX844030PC brochure to prove R&S superiority, because the Anritsu comparison page says that brochure can describe Anritsu products but cannot verify R&S advantage claims [18].
You need validation reports, test-case lists, option codes, versions, and accreditation or certification evidence for PTCRB / GCF / operator-acceptance claims, because the Amarisoft battle card lacks those details for R&S aligned tests and Samsung-related NTN validation claims [20].
You must not equate CMX500 RF pre-conformance with strict conformance or certification, because the RF pre-conformance page says strict RF conformance testing and validated test cases use the R&S TS8980 Conformance Test Platform [50].
You need formal test setup, DUT, band combination, software release, and report evidence for throughput or performance claims, because the CMX500 callbox unresolved section says the 10.6 Gbps and 10 Gbps claims lack those details [37].
You need formal datasheets or verified test reports for FR1 / FR2 / FR3 bandwidth and data-rate comparisons, because the Anritsu comparison page flags bandwidth and data-rate limitations and contradictions as requiring formal validation [18].
You need formal test setup, option, fixture, frequency, and sales-kit content for AI-server mapping claims, because the AI-server R&S solution mapping table explicitly says those details are not provided [3].
You need official competitor support, warranty, calibration, and footprint evidence before using those as differentiators, because the Amarisoft unresolved page says “no global footprint,” “remote-only support,” and similar claims require Amarisoft official or third-party confirmation [89].
